glance.question: Can women be pastors and elders, and which other roles are open to them?

positions.name: Complementarianism
positions.claim: Equal in dignity, distinct in role: pastors and elders are men.

positions.name: Egalitarianism
positions.claim: Every ministry and office is open to women and men alike.

positions.name: Soft Complementarianism / Third Way
positions.claim: Only the pastoral office is reserved for men; most teaching roles are open.

start_here.title: What Does It Mean That Women Should “Remain Quiet” in Church? (1 Timothy 2)
start_here.author: Denny Burk
start_here.why: A careful complementarian reading of the passage the whole debate turns on.

start_here.title: Complementarian at Home, Egalitarian at Church? Paul Would Approve.
start_here.author: Gordon P. Hugenberger
start_here.why: Argues the main passages may be more about marriage than ministry.

start_here.title: Even Egalitarian Churches Limit Women's Leadership
start_here.author: Rachel Heim Rausch
start_here.why: An egalitarian look at the gap between what churches affirm and what they practice.

key_number.text: 44% of evangelical pastors say a woman could be senior pastor at their church; 84% say she could teach a coed adult Bible study.
key_number.study: Leadership Roles of Women Divide Protestant Denominations
